The designed-to-fail e2e assertion test_pipeline_e2e_effective_timeout now passes; all 3 existing consumer unit tests stay green; producer.py, engine.py, and all three existing test files are byte-identical to baseline (git diff vs baseline touches only pipeline/consumer.py plus the tracked .pyc artifact).

verified_facts: consumer.job_timeout final resolution order (as implemented): if 'timeout_ms' in job: return job['timeout_ms']; elif 'timeout' in job: return job['timeout']; else: return DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000). Values are returned raw (no conversion); all branches yield int milliseconds for C1-conformant jobs.

consumer.job_timeout(producer.make_job('j1', {'cmd': 'x'}, timeout_ms=500)) == 500, asserted green by tests.test_pipeline_e2e.TestPipelineE2E.test_pipeline_e2e_effective_timeout (the fixture's designed-to-fail e2e assertion).

Observed behaviors: job_timeout({'timeout': 123}) == 123 (draft-key fallback preserved, keeps test_job_timeout_reads_consumer_key green); job_timeout({}) == 30000 (default branch, no exception); job_timeout({'timeout_ms': 500, 'timeout': 123}) == 500 (timeout_ms wins per C1 precedence).
